mappings.note: Calorific values of solid/liquid/gaseous fuels; the four sub-questions ask what LPG stands for, which fuel has the highest calorific value, and which fuels are dung cake and CNG. This is SOURCES OF ENERGY, not Our Environment, and the chapter's frame has nothing for it: C 2.8-LO-1/LO-2 are food chains and the ten per cent law, C 4.1-LO-1 is biodegradable vs non-biodegradable, C 4.3-LO-2/LO-3 are ozone and waste disposal. Not even C 2.8 fits, because nothing is asked about an earth system -- the item is entirely fuel properties. Cited at the goal, CG 2 'Explores the physical world around them, and understands scientific principles and laws', which is the only true statement the frame supports. Its stored concept tag 'Waste Management Strategies' is unrelated to what the item asks.

Alternative energy sources: windmills and wind turbines, geothermal, solar cell, solar panel. Again SOURCES OF ENERGY rather than Our Environment. It is one step nearer the frame than item 188 -- the passage opens by contrasting fossil fuel with alternatives, and geothermal is a geosphere phenomenon named in C 2.8 -- but the four sub-questions asked are pure recall of an energy source's name, with no earth-system interaction to analyse, so C 2.8 would overstate what is tested. Cited at CG 2 for the same reason as 188. Distinct from 188 only in subject matter, not in code, because the frame offers no finer distinction here.
